headline: Iran Claims a Supertanker Sank After a Hormuz Mine Strike
deck: The Revolutionary Guards’ account names neither vessel nor crew; the claimed cargo and any change in physical oil flow remain unconfirmed.
body: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards say two oil tankers attempting to transit via routes they called unauthorised struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and that one sank. [E3] The Guards said the vessel was a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude and that it sank after an explosion and fire. [E4]

The New Arab reported that no independent confirmation of the incidents had been provided. [E2] Anadolu said the Iranian statement did not identify either vessel or give crew details. [E5] The vessel identity, the claimed cargo and any physical effect on oil flows therefore remain unconfirmed.
This is a later Iranian claim than the paper’s 15 November report, which said Iranian naval forces and the Guards had reported fires on three oil tankers after mine strikes. [E6]
Dawn separately reported an IRGC statement declaring the Strait of Hormuz closed. [E1]

evidence_box.fragment: “The US air defence radar system at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain was targeted by six drones belonging to the IRGC Aerospace Force,” the Guards said in a statement posted by the state broadcaster on Telegram. “The Strait of Hormuz is closed, and any aggression by the American enemy will be met with an even harsher and more forceful response,” it added.
